name: Taohong Siwu decoction (Chinese herbal formula)
short: Mostly add-on trial reviews: angina (12 trials), no serious adverse events reported, no death data; with heparin after hip surgery (18 trials), no significant rise in adverse events, no bleeding data.
text: Safety evidence for Taohong Siwu decoction comes from meta-analyses of trials in which it was mostly added to other treatment; the cited abstracts do not list its herbs or give adverse-event figures. In a meta-analysis of 12 trials (959 patients with angina) of the decoction plus conventional treatment, no serious adverse events were reported, and none of the included studies reported the review's main outcome, a combined measure of death, heart attack and repeat artery procedures, so the review cannot show whether these events occurred. In a 2024 meta-analysis of 18 randomized trials (1,353 patients having hip fracture surgery or hip replacement), adding the decoction to low-molecular-weight heparin (a blood-thinning medicine) did not significantly increase adverse events, and blood clotting times (PT and APTT) did not differ significantly from heparin alone, but the abstract does not report bleeding events; the authors note small samples and low-quality evidence. A 2022 meta-analysis of 9 trials (827 patients with high blood pressure) reported fewer adverse reactions when the decoction was added to blood-pressure medicines, and its authors call for higher-quality studies because of biased results. Apart from the clotting-time results with heparin, no interaction data were found in the cited sources.
